title: महानन्द ढकालको सिमाना मुक्तक सङ्ग्रहमा सबाल्टर्न {The Subaltern in Mahananda Dhakal's Simana Muktaka collection}
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेख महानन्द ढकालको सिमाना मुक्तक सङ्ग्रहमा सबाल्टर्न अध्ययन गरिएको छ । सबाल्टर्न वर्गहितप्रति समर्पित रहेर  वर्तमान साहित्य र समालोचनाको क्षेत्रमा विकसित नवीन मान्यता भएकाले यससँग सम्बद्ध सैद्धान्तिक आधारमा मुक्तकहरूको अध्ययन गर्न लागिएको हो । सबाल्टर्न अध्ययनलाई उच्च विवादको बीचबाट र आलोचनात्मक पृष्टभूमीको गर्भबाट हुर्किएको अभियान मानिन्छ । भारतबाट विकसित भएर विभिन्न मुलुकमा फैलिएको यो अध्ययनपद्धति भएकाले पूर्वबाट पश्चिम फैलिएको सशक्त अभियान मानिएका छ । सबाल्टर्न अध्ययनमा विभिन्न जातजति, महिला, दलित, पिछडिएका क्षेत्र र सीमान्तकृत वर्गको बोली साथै इतिहासबाट बहिष्कृत भएकाको पहिचनको खोजी गरिन्छ । यस लेखमा पनि निम्नवर्गीय सबाल्टर्न वर्गको समस्यालाई पहिल्याउने र उनीहरूले भोग्नु परेको अन्याय, अत्याचार, अधिनस्थ भएको अवस्था साथै विद्रोहका स्वरलाई समेटिएको छ । यसमा प्राथमिक र द्वितीयक स्रोतका सामग्रीको सङ्कलनका लागि पुस्तकालयीय पद्धतिको उपयोग गरिएको छ र सबाल्टर्नसँग सम्बन्धित सैद्धान्तिक ढाँचा तयार गरेर निगमन विधिबाट मुक्तकहरूको विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । यसमा राज्यव्यवस्था र सबाल्टर्नको अवस्था, वर्गीय सबाल्टर्न साथै सबाल्टर्न वर्गको प्रतिकार र विद्रोहलाई अध्ययनको विषय बनाइएको छ । यस अध्ययनले उच्चशिक्षा अध्ययन गर्ने विद्यार्थी, शोधकर्ता र प्रज्ञिक क्षेत्रमा जिज्ञासा राख्ने व्यक्तिहरूलाई नवीन ज्ञान प्रदान गर्नेछ । यस आलेखमा ढकालको सिमाना मुक्तक सङ्ग्रहमा सबाल्टर्नको विषयवस्तुमा मूलतः राज्यव्यवस्था साथै वर्गीय आधारमा सबाल्टर्न वर्गलाई अधीनस्थ बनाइएको हुनाले दुःख, पीडा र असमानताको अन्त्यका लागि प्रतिकार र विद्रोह गरेको अवस्था प्रस्तुत गरिएको निष्कर्ष रहेको छ ।
american_english: This paper studies the subaltern in Mahananda Dhakal's Simana Muktaka collection. The subaltern is dedicated to class struggle, and the recent development of new recognitions in the field of literature and criticism has made it possible to study the muktakas based on the associated theoretical foundation. Subaltern studies are considered an effective campaign that emerged from above controversy and against a critical background. This approach, developed in India and spread to various countries, is seen as a powerful campaign that spread from East to West. Subaltern studies focus on identifying various castes, women, Dalits, backward regions, and marginalized classes, as well as their voices and histories that have been excluded. This paper also covers the problems of the lower-class subaltern, the injustices they suffer, their oppressed state, and their rebellion against it. It uses the library method for the collection of primary and secondary source materials and analyzes the muktakas using a deductive method based on the theoretical framework related to subaltern. The study covers the state system and the condition of subalterns, as well as the class-based subalterns and their resistance and rebellion. This study will provide new knowledge to students, researchers, and scholars interested in higher education. The paper's main finding is that the lower-class subaltern in Dhakal's Simana Muktaka collection is presented in a state of suffering, pain, and inequality due to being subjugated by the state system and class structure, leading to resistance and rebellion to end their suffering.
british_english: This paper investigates the subaltern within Mahananda Dhakal's Simana Muktaka collection. Dedicated to class struggle, recent developments in literary and critical theory have facilitated the study of muktakas based on a related theoretical framework. Subaltern studies are viewed as an effective campaign emerging from high-level controversy and a critical background. Originating in India, this methodology has spread across various countries, becoming a powerful East-to-West movement. The studies examine different castes, women, Dalits, backward regions, and marginalized classes, alongside their voices and histories often excluded from historical narratives. This paper also addresses the challenges faced by lower-class subalterns, including injustices, oppression, and their subsequent resistance and rebellion. Utilising library research for primary and secondary sources, the analysis employs a deductive method grounded in subaltern-related theoretical constructs. The study explores the state apparatus, the condition of subalterns, class-based subalterns, and their acts of resistance and rebellion, aiming to offer new insights for higher education students, researchers, and scholars. The key conclusion is that lower-class subalterns in Dhakal's Simana Muktaka collection are depicted as enduring suffering, pain, and inequality due to their subjugation by state and class structures, prompting resistance and rebellion to alleviate their plight.
